paper.title: MLREF: Efficient Module Reuse for Reward Design in Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models
paper.source_version: arXiv v1, submitted 2026-08-19 11:36:55 UTC; sole public revision verified 2026-08-30; PDF SHA-256 bfdaf574bb3c241d046be9d447ef2cdceebd0adab387ff77411a668f41863aff; TeX-source SHA-256 eae7c2d2600e2f07009a84ef3534d9ef2a9b183c9f4fd06e2c14cef685462852. No official project or code URL is supplied in v1 or its source archive, so no implementation revision is pinned.

decision_relevance.why_admitted: MLREF directly evolves executable task rewards while keeping each task-local policy-training setup fixed. Its persistent module pool, typed edit operations, component-level credit heuristic, matched candidate budget, and explicit rollback provide transferable reward-harness interfaces; its formal separation of candidate reward from policy fitness also motivates an independent evaluator contract.
not_evidence_for: reference-motion selection, ordering, composition, transition, recovery, or certification
a reference-conditioned policy, reference oracle, OGMP state machine, or playback clock
cross-task transfer of reward modules; reuse is demonstrated only across iterations within a task
natural-language human steering or preference translation
foundation-controller, VIBE, humanoid motion-tracking, or physical-robot integration
causal contribution of an individual module from reward-performance correlation
safe, deterministic, bounded, or side-effect-free execution of LLM-generated Python
an exact reproducible implementation of the printed UCB selector
a complete frozen MDP, controller, software, and dependency manifest

mechanisms.name: Persistent reward-module pool
mechanisms.description: The persistent optimization object is a pool of named reward modules. A reward function is only a temporary linear combination assembled from selected pool members, so successful modules can survive the function and iteration that introduced them.

mechanisms.name: Reflection-guided module generation
mechanisms.description: Initial task reflection identifies success, useful or harmful behavior, and non-obvious strategies; environment reflection extracts available variable names, types, shapes, and descriptions. Later reflection compares prior and best pools and their outcomes, or analyzes a training error trace, before the LLM plans another pool variant.

mechanisms.name: Specification-first modules and typed pool edits
mechanisms.description: Initialization separates module specification from implementation. Each specification names the module, typed input variables, and intended behavior; later plans apply add, delete/remove, modify-code-under-fixed-specification, or rewrite-specification-and-code operations with rationales.

mechanisms.name: Hybrid semantic and correlation credit
mechanisms.description: Each module receives an LLM credit from normalized proposed weights and a correlation credit from lagged Pearson correlations between its reward curve and the policy-performance curve, including raw and slow-difference series. Both are EMA-smoothed, normalized, and fused into a composite score.

mechanisms.name: UCB-selected linear reward assembly
mechanisms.description: A UCB bonus augments each fused module score to explore underused modules. The top-K modules are selected, and their fused composite scores become the non-negative weights in the executable linear reward combination.

mechanisms.name: Thresholded merge with rollback
mechanisms.description: Parallel pool variants more than margin t below the historical best are discarded. Surviving modules are unioned, same-name collisions retain the best-performing version, and a round with no survivor restores the prior pool while preserving failed attempts for reflection.

mechanisms.name: Task-local fixed-trainer reward search
mechanisms.description: Each candidate reward trains PPO in the same task-local environment configuration for 3,000 epochs and returns fitness plus module traces to the reward-design loop. After selection, the final reward trains a policy from scratch for 20,000 epochs on five seeds; the reference/oracle surface is not changed.

failure_modes.name: Invalid generated code can crash RL training
failure_modes.description: The paper explicitly states that LLM hallucination can produce invalid code that crashes RL training. MLREF reacts to the returned error trace during feedback reflection rather than documenting a pre-execution proof of safety or validity.

failure_modes.name: Pool redundancy and conflicting incentives
failure_modes.description: The authors identify naive pool accumulation as a source of redundant or conflicting incentives. The merge rule resolves same-name versions by performance, but v1 does not define semantic deduplication for differently named modules.

failure_modes.name: Correlation credit is not causal attribution
failure_modes.description: Lagged Pearson correlation between a module reward curve and the policy-performance curve is associational: policy learning, other modules, and changing assemblies can affect both. No module-level intervention study validates the individual credit scores causally.

failure_modes.name: Printed UCB selector is self-ambiguous
failure_modes.description: Appendix A.3 prints u_i as the UCB score on the left while also defining u_i as the module's selection count in the denominator and prose, then says modules are ranked by u_i. No official code is linked to disambiguate the implementation.

failure_modes.name: Merge-margin units are unspecified
failure_modes.description: The fixed soft-update threshold is t=0.1, but v1 does not state whether the task-local fitness is normalized before applying the margin or otherwise define its units. This prevents an exact cross-task implementation contract.

failure_modes.name: Sparse-reward manipulation remains weak
failure_modes.description: The authors call MLREF's absolute Block Stack performance modest despite its improvement over baselines and identify early exploration versus progressive exploitation as unresolved.

failure_modes.name: Strong LLM-backbone dependence
failure_modes.description: Replacing DeepSeek-V4-Flash with GPT-4o yields only 40.9 percent of full MLREF performance in the three-task ablation. The main experiments use one proprietary API model label, and open-source LLMs are left for future evaluation.

failure_modes.name: Best-of-three selection without outer-loop uncertainty
failure_modes.description: MLREF returns the best of three complete stochastic pipeline runs. The paper reports five-seed final-policy means and standard deviations but not variance across reward-search executions, aggregate confidence intervals, or significance tests.

failure_modes.name: Validation-to-test claim is under-specified
failure_modes.description: The authors state that only full MLREF's validation-selected reward remains best at test on all three ablation tasks, but v1 does not define the validation/test construction, split sizes, selection noise, or separate scores.

failure_modes.name: Prompt contract is not an execution-safety boundary
failure_modes.description: The prompts require a typed single-function TorchScript-compatible reward, but v1 documents no sandbox, static allowlist, purity check, resource bound, bounded-output check, or pre-execution semantic validator.

failure_modes.name: No code, exact model snapshot, or complete runtime pin
failure_modes.description: The paper supplies formulas, prompts, and top-level hyperparameters, but no official code URL, implementation revision, dependency lock, environment manifest, exact DeepSeek API snapshot, sampling temperature, or LLM seed; PPO details are inherited by reference to EUREKA.

failure_modes.name: Simulation-only and reward-only scope
failure_modes.description: All reported tasks are from Isaac Gym or Bi-DexHands. There is no physical-robot, safety, perturbation-recovery, cross-MDP transfer, reference-composition, or oracle experiment.

evaluation.name: Matched outer-loop candidate budget
evaluation.description: Three MLREF executions of nine iterations and three variants produce 81 candidate-policy trainings per task, compared with 80 EUREKA candidates and 80 RF-Agent MCTS updates. Every candidate receives 3,000 epochs.

evaluation.name: Seventeen-task final-policy comparison
evaluation.description: After five-seed 20,000-epoch PPO retraining from scratch, MLREF reports a 3.288 normalized average on seven paper-labelled locomotion tasks versus RF-Agent's 2.625, and a 0.708 average on ten manipulation tasks versus EUREKA's 0.664. MLREF has the best individual mean on four and two tasks respectively.

evaluation.name: Three-task mechanism and model ablation
evaluation.description: On Ant, Block Stack, and Bottle Cap, no pool, no reflection, and no weight optimization average 73.2, 53.3, and 63.9 percent of full MLREF; GPT-4o averages 40.9 percent. Bottle Cap is a negative exception where no pool scores 0.988 versus full MLREF's 0.987.

evaluation.name: Best-sample evolution curves
evaluation.description: The authors compare the best candidate at each normalized progress point and report smoother MLREF trajectories on the all-task average, Shadow Hand, and Catch Abreast. MLREF curves use the best variant among three independent runs; all-task curves min-max normalize each task before averaging.

evaluation.name: Three-task validation-to-test observation
evaluation.description: The paper states that on all three ablation tasks, only full MLREF consistently keeps the validation-selected reward best at test, while ablated variants frequently underperform. No split construction or separate numeric test table is reported.

evaluation.name: Public artifact reproducibility audit
evaluation.description: The exact arXiv v1 PDF and source are pinned and include formulas, prompts, and hyperparameters. They include no official code/project URL; the printed UCB notation is ambiguous and the DeepSeek API model is not snapshot-pinned.

evidence.locator: Submission header and history; official v1 PDF and TeX-source bytes retrieved 2026-08-30
evidence.claim: The title, authors, arXiv ID, submission timestamp, 22-page/5-figure/4-table metadata, sole v1 history, and exact reviewed PDF/source hashes identify the public paper artifact.

Function-level reward search loses effective components; naive module accumulation can create redundancy or conflicting incentives; MLREF instead uses a persistent named pool, per-module credit, semantic guidance, and explicit rollback.
The formal reward-design problem separates fixed environment E and policy optimizer A, candidate reward R, trained policy pi_R, and policy fitness F.

MLREF assembles a temporary weighted linear reward from persistent pool modules, trains parallel candidates, merges or rolls back using fitness, reflects on feedback, and returns the best reward across iterations.

Module metadata contains name, typed inputs, and intended-function description; initialization separates specification from code, and improvement uses add, delete, modify, and rewrite operations with rationales.

Variants more than margin t below historical best are discarded; survivor modules are unioned, same-name collisions retain the best-performing version, and no survivor triggers rollback while failures enter later reflection.
Task, environment, and feedback reflection precede generation; the paper states that hallucinated invalid code can crash RL training and that an error trace is analyzed after failure.

Module selection fuses normalized LLM weight credit with lagged raw/difference Pearson correlation credit, applies EMA smoothing and a UCB exploration bonus, and uses selected modules' fused scores as reward weights.

evidence.locator: Appendix A.3, UCB equation and immediately following prose
evidence.claim: The published equation and prose reuse u_i as both the UCB score and module selection count, then use u_i as the ranking quantity, leaving the selector notation self-ambiguous.

Table 4 reports I=9, S=3, three runs, five final seeds, t=0.1, correlation and fusion settings, gamma=0.2, K=5, PPO, 3,000/20,000 epochs, DeepSeek-V4-Flash reasoning mode, and 80-evaluation baseline budgets.
The prompts request 4-6 initial module specifications and one typed Python function per module returning torch.Tensor with TorchScript-compatible code and matched specification inputs.

MLREF chooses the best of three complete 9-by-3 pipelines; candidates train 3,000 epochs, selected rewards retrain PPO from scratch for 20,000 epochs on five seeds, DeepSeek-V4-Flash serves all main calls, and environment settings follow EUREKA.

Across 17 Isaac Gym/Bi-DexHands tasks, MLREF reports 3.288 versus 2.625 best-baseline normalized locomotion average and 0.708 versus 0.664 best-baseline manipulation average, with full per-task means and standard deviations.

The Ant/Block Stack/Bottle Cap ablation reports GPT-4o, no-pool, no-reflection, and no-weight-optimization results and states that only full MLREF consistently retains its validation-selected reward as best at test across the three tasks.

Evolution plots use the best sample per iteration, the best MLREF variant across three runs, normalized progress axes, and per-task min-max normalization for the all-task average; the authors interpret MLREF as more stable than baselines.
The authors identify modest absolute performance on sparse Block Stack, narrow LLM coverage including no open-source models, and the single-LLM design as limitations.
